title: 1985 AHSME Problem 6
statement: One student in a class of boys and girls is to be chosen to represent the class. Each student is equally likely to be chosen and the probability that a boy is chosen is \(\frac23\) of the probability that a girl is chosen. The ratio of the number of boys to the total number of boys and girls is

solutions.text:
Because every student is equally likely to be selected, the number of boys is \(\frac{2}{3}\) of the number of girls. Thus the boys-to-girls ratio is \(2:3,\) and boys make up \(\frac{2}{2+3}=\frac{2}{5}\) of the class.

Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: Equal likelihood makes the selection probabilities proportional to the class counts
A boys-to-girls ratio of \(2:3\) uses five equal parts in all
